note: A coordinate that only survives at full binary64 precision (section 8). The expected values here are JSON numbers in this same file, so a reader that compares them compares doubles rather than text, which is the right test: -3.6712345678901234 and -3.6712345678901235 are the SAME double (0xc00d5eb03aa8431e). What it proves is narrower than it looks, and saying so is the point of this note. The accept tier applies the precision rules of section 4.1 to both sides before it compares, so a reader that parsed this literal one bit wrong would have the error normalised away and stay green. The case proves the reader accepts a seventeen-digit literal and does not mangle it visibly: it does not truncate the number, refuse it, or put it in the wrong channel. This is a reader-preservation case and not a writer example. No conforming writer emits these values, because section 4.1 has a writer round coordinates to 6 places and elevations to 1 at the emit boundary. Encoding this document through a writer gives -3.671235, and that is correct.
